sanity_expectations: At t=0, because V starts at resting_voltage and A=0, the leak and adaptation terms vanish so dV/dt initially equals applied_current/membrane_capacitance = 120 in model units; this is an exact check from the inherited initial conditions and chosen parameters.

During sustained depolarization, membrane_capacitance should rise above its baseline 1.0 toward a depolarization-dependent target, so later voltage changes under the same current step should be slower than the earliest charging phase.

A should increase from 0 only when V exceeds resting_voltage, then approach a finite depolarization-dependent level rather than growing linearly without bound; stronger depolarization within the trajectory should show diminishing extra recruitment because adaptation_saturation_scale is 15 mV.

G should start at 1 and decline only after sustained depolarization above rest; with adaptation_inactivation_gain=0.5 it should remain positive and approach a reduced availability rather than collapse to zero.
The V-to-dV/dt relation should bend downward more strongly at larger depolarization than near rest because leak_rectification_strength is nonzero.

Compared at similar depolarized V and nonzero A reached later in the same trajectory, the effective adaptation suppression of dV/dt should be weaker than earlier because G has fallen; this is the observable contrast added by the new state and is absent if adaptation_inactivation_gain were zero.

rationale: Using the provided typed ODE contract, the governing law must be sampled as a four-state system over time only, with V as target_state and A, membrane_capacitance, and G retained as dynamic states. The chosen constant depolarizing drive is strong enough to move V several to a few tens of mV above rest without intentionally pushing everything into an extreme saturation/recovery limit. This exposes the recorded mechanisms in one sustained-step trajectory family: (i) leak rectification is visible because leak_rectification_strength is nonzero but modest, so the passive outward term bends downward progressively with depolarization rather than dominating immediately; (ii) adaptation recruitment saturates on a 15 mV depolarization scale, so moderate depolarization recruits A substantially while stronger depolarization shows diminishing incremental recruitment instead of indefinite linear growth; (iii) dynamic membrane capacitance is history-dependent but not frozen, because baseline_membrane_capacitance=1 and capacitance_recruitment_gain=0.6 with a 150 ms time constant allow later slowing relative to early charging during the same sustained drive; (iv) the added availability state G is preserved as declared by the freedom_change add_state decision and is not collapsed back to a parameter. With adaptation_inactivation_gain=0.5, adaptation_inactivation_scale=12 mV, and adaptation_availability_time_constant=250 ms, prolonged depolarization can reduce adaptation efficacy noticeably but not eliminate it, enabling the intended early-vs-late contrast where similar V and A can correspond to weaker adaptation effect later because G has declined. Time range to 600 ms covers several adaptation/capacitance/availability timescales enough to show onset, transition, and approach toward a later phase while remaining biologically plausible for a subthreshold current step. Weak effects honestly noted: at very early times A and G-mediated modulation are inactive because A(0)=0 and G(0)=1 by inherited initial conditions; near rest the rectification and saturation nonlinearities are mild, approximating the parent locally.
